ov: Nocturnal freshwater fish of South America that stun prey with electric shocks; in 2019 they were split into three species. They must breathe air, gulping it about every two minutes, have poor eyesight, and find their way by electrolocation.

why.dg: Its shocks reach 860 volts, strong enough to drive off animals as large as horses.
why.ac: Nocturnal, with poor eyesight made up for by sensing electric fields.

fx: Studies of electric eels in the 1770s helped lead to the invention of the battery in 1800.
Because it breathes air, it can live in water that is low in oxygen.
_t: Is an Electric Eel Dangerous? Diet, Size & Quick Facts
